findings.rule_description: Provider shall protect clients from abuse, prevent abuse
findings.finding_text: The provider was out of compliance with R380-80-5(4) by not protecting clients from harm or mistreatment and any action that may compromise the health and safety through acts or omissions and shall instruct and encourage others to do the same. During the investigation inspection, the evidence substantiated that on November 4, 2025, staff members harmed a client by forcibly removing a client from the top bunk of a bed. During the unnecessary physical restraint, a staff member pulled the client downward, causing the client’s head to strike the staff member’s knee and subsequently hit the floor; the client incurred a concussion.

findings.rule_description: Provider shall comply with policies and safe practices
findings.finding_text: The provider was out of compliance with R380-80-5(3) by not complying with applicable and safe practices that address the appropriate treatment of clients. During the investigation, the evidence substantiated that two staff members failed to comply with the provider’s behavior management policy and procedure by conducting a physical restraint on a client who was not a harm to themselves or others, for staff convenience.

findings.rule_description: Application submitted within 2 weeks and applicant directly supervised
findings.finding_text: The provider was out of compliance with R501-14-5(2)(a) by not submitting a background check for an individual associated with the license within two weeks. During the file review, a staff member that had access to clients did not have a background check.

The provider was out of compliance with R380-600-7(16)(a) by not reporting a critical incident withing one business day. During the inspection a client was placed in a restraint and this was not reported to Licensing. This is a repeat noncompliance as noted on 5/28/2025, 2/7/2024 and 1/18/2024.

The provider was out of compliance with R501-1-16(1)(p) by not ensuring that a staff member received their full pre-service training within 30 days. During the inspection a staff file revealed that a staff member did not receive their appropriate use of seclusion training within 30 days. This is a repeat noncompliance as noted on 8/6/2024 and 1/11/2024.

findings.finding_text: The provider was out of compliance with R501-1-8(1)(a) due to not maintaining a clean building so that it is free from health hazards. During the inspection, evidence substantiated that multiple kitchen areas failed to meet sanitary standards. Specifically, the general kitchen area, the floor of the walk-in refrigerator, and the space beneath the kitchen sink were heavily soiled and required deep cleaning. This is a repeat rule noncompliance as noted on January 25, 2024. Technical Assistance was given on October 16, 2025.

findings.rule_description: Provider is responsible for their own staff's compliance
findings.finding_text: The provider was out of compliance with R380-80-3(1) for failing to comply with each applicable federal, state, and local law, and each policy and administrative rule required by the department or by other state and federal agencies that regulate or oversee the provider’s programs. Investigative interviews indicate that the provider enforced restrictive calling policies that unlawfully blocked client communication with the Ombuds office. While the Ombudsman contact details were physically posted on-site, clients were not permitted to make unapproved outbound calls, and staff actively refused at least one client's request to contact the Ombudsman.

The provider was out of compliance with R501-19-5(1)(b)((ii) and (iii) for not ensuring the manager has a bachelor's degree or equivalent training in a human service-related field and has at least three years management experience in a residential or secure treatment setting. During the investigation, a credential review revealed that eight (8) provider Program Managers do not meet the requirements for their position.

The provider was out of compliance with 26B-2-123(6)(a)(i) for failing to facilitate confidential voice-to-voice communication between a child and the child’s parents, guardian, foster parents, and siblings, as applicable. During the inspection, multiple client interviews confirmed that clients' weekly phone calls are conducted publicly and monitored by staff. The provider verified the practice, demonstrating that calls occur in a common area where staff remain within earshot to supervise the unit and are able to overhear conversations.

The provider was out of compliance with R380-80-4(1) for not protecting a client from mistreatment. During the inspection, video evidence showed a staff member grabbing the top of a client’s hair with his hand, bending his fingers around her hair at the root, and holding onto it in order to push the client’s head back and hold it in place.
